papers.title_en: SARIA: Persistence-Aware KV Caching with Coordinated DRAM--SSD Reload for LLM Agents
papers.authors: Hui Li, Qihui Zhou, Xiao Yan, Shumeng Zhang, Zijie Dai, Zequn Gong, Mingcong Song, Guoping Long, Hongjie Si, James Cheng
papers.evidence: 面向LLM智能体的KV缓存选择性准入与重载
papers.tldr: 多轮LLM智能体复用长上下文前缀，KV缓存对降低预填延迟很关键，但DRAM容量有限，SSD扩展又带来写放大和重载带宽瓶颈。SARIA利用会话级时间局部性联合管理DRAM与SSD：写路径按驱逐与复用历史选择性持久化，读路径将SSD命中块预填后提升至DRAM，并由传输协调器共享GPU入口带宽。在LMCache MP及TraceLab、WEKA负载上，SSD写减少57.1–58.9%，TTFT较纯DRAM缓存降低42.3–79.7%。
papers.abstract_en: Multi-turn LLM agents usually reuse long context prefixes, making key value (KV) caching crucial for reducing prefill latency. SSDs provide a low-cost extension to limited DRAM capacity but introduce two key challenges. Eagerly persisting all KV cache blocks incurs substantial write traffic and rapidly consumes finite SSD endurance. Meanwhile, the small number of SSDs provisioned in typical GPU servers limits aggregate reload bandwidth, making SSD-resident KV cache much slower to retrieve than that in DRAM and inflating prefill latency.   We present \textsc{Saria} (Selective Admission and Reload for Inference Acceleration), a KV caching system that jointly manages DRAM and SSD by exploiting the session-level temporal locality of LLM agents to reduce SSD writes and accelerate cache reload. On the write path, \textsc{Saria} uses eviction and reuse history to selectively persist KV cache blocks that exhibit reuse opportunities beyond their DRAM residency, avoiding unnecessary writes for KV cache already hosted in DRAM. On the read path, \textsc{Saria} promotes selected SSD-hit KV cache blocks from GPU memory into DRAM after prefill, allowing subsequent reuse within the same session to reduce SSD read traffic while limiting DRAM contention. A transfer coordinator paces DRAM reads while SSD transfers are active, allowing both paths to make progress and efficiently share GPU ingress bandwidth.   We implement \textsc{Saria} on LMCache MP and evaluate it using workloads from TraceLab and WEKA, covering both full-attention and hybrid-attention models. The results show that \textsc{Saria} reduces SSD writes by 57.1--58.9\% compared with popular full duplicate caching and the mean time to first token (TTFT) by 42.3--79.7\% over DRAM-only caching.

papers.title_en: SPECMEM: Accelerating Agentic Tool Calling via Live Memory Management
papers.authors: Zihe Song, Wenting Zhao, Ye Liu, Yuanjie Zhu, Ke Xu, Shanghao Li, Philip S. Yu
papers.evidence: 按用户有界存储工具调用记忆并采用LRU驱逐，属于智能体侧缓存淘汰策略
papers.tldr: 工具调用智能体部署成本主要在自回归解码延迟，投机解码可无损加速，但现有系统缺乏跨会话记忆或草稿库构建后不再更新。SpecMem将已验证调用在线写回有界每用户存储并用LRU淘汰，配合副作用门控延迟不可逆调用。在多会话多用户流上，冻结存储接受率持续下降，SpecMem保持稳定，平均接受token高27%，墙钟加速最高1.74倍。其贡献在于把工具调用记忆作为部署期持续管理对象。
papers.abstract_en: Tool-calling agents are mostly optimized for accuracy; in deployment, however, their growing cost is latency: every tool call is decoded autoregressively. Speculative decoding accelerates this without changing the output, and retrieved past calls make strong drafts under real use, where each user's behavior tends to repeat. Yet existing systems keep no cross-session memory, or build the draft store once and never update it. We propose SpecMem, a tool-call memory kept alive and managed throughout deployment: verified calls are written back online into bounded per-user stores with LRU eviction, and a side-effect gate defers irreversible calls until verification confirms. On multi-session, multi-user query streams served by three open-weight models, a frozen store steadily loses acceptance while SpecMem holds it: a 27% gap in mean accepted tokens (+11% to +34% across benchmarks, tracking how much novel work arrives after the store is built) and up to 1.74x wall-clock speedup. Ablations attribute the gain almost entirely to keeping the store live; local per-user scoping adds no acceptance but closes a measured cross-user leakage channel, and gating on declared side effects, rather than on retrieval confidence, is what eliminates irreversible mistakes.

papers.title_en: Adaptive Deadline- and Energy-Aware Caching Algorithms in Dynamic Multi-UAV Edge Networks
papers.evidence: 多无人机网络中截止时间与能量感知的缓存放置与替换
papers.tldr: 多无人机边缘网络需在基础设施受损时维持内容分发，但现有缓存策略难以兼顾时空异构需求、内容截止期和机间通信能耗均衡。论文将缓存放置与替换建模为动态截止期与能耗感知问题，先提出可解释分层规则方法DE-UBAC，再提出融合局部/全局GRU时序表征和集中式PPO的GRU-DEPPO。仿真中GRU-DEPPO取得最低截止期错失率和UAV侧通信总能耗，较DE-UBAC错失率约降61%、机间能耗不均衡约降40%。
papers.abstract_en: Content caching via unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) becomes one of the solutions to maintain content delivery when terrestrial infrastructure is unavailable or disrupted. However, existing caching approaches often focus primarily on cache-hit performance or average delivery delay, without jointly addressing spatially heterogeneous and time-varying demand, content-specific deadlines, and uneven communication-energy consumption across UAVs. To address these challenges, we formulate a dynamic deadline- and energy-aware cache placement and replacement problem that jointly considers deadline misses, UAV-side communication energy, and inter-UAV energy imbalance. To achieve this, we first develop deadline- and energy-aware UBAC (DE-UBAC), an interpretable hierarchical rule-based realization that incorporates deadline-aware prioritization, cooperative placement, energy-aware coordination, and cache-update cost. However, predefined priorities and thresholds limit its adaptability under dynamically coupled network conditions. We therefore propose GRU-assisted Deadline- and Energy-aware Proximal Policy Optimization (GRU-DEPPO), which combines local and global GRU-based temporal representations with a centralized PPO actor-critic for adaptive cache placement and replacement. Simulation results show that GRU-DEPPO achieves the lowest deadline-miss rate and total UAV-side communication energy among the considered schemes. Compared with DE-UBAC, GRU-DEPPO reduces the deadline-miss rate by approximately 61% and inter-UAV energy imbalance by approximately 40%.

papers.title_en: REM: What to Store, When to Recall, What to Forget in Experience Memory for Coding Agents
papers.authors: Xinyi Lisa Chen, Pedro Herrero-Vidal, Xiaohan Chen, Xiaojing Yu, Cris Liu, Bingqing Song, Bin Xu, Suleiman A. Khan, You-Lin Chen
papers.evidence: 智能体循环内关于存什么、何时召回与遗忘什么的记忆生命周期决策
papers.tldr: LLM智能体在仓库级编程等长程任务中积累经验，但现有记忆系统只重检索，无法判断何时需要与保留多久。REM在think-act循环内管理记忆生命周期，显式决定存什么、何时召回、何时遗忘：轨迹压缩为阶段化文档，任务开始时注入，受阻时才提供实现记录，一次曝光后驱逐。在SWE-ContextBench Lite上匹配@1达68.7%，解决率27.6%，成本降17%。这表明经验复用瓶颈在存储与生命周期治理，而非检索精度。
papers.abstract_en: Large language model (LLM) agents now autonomously complete long-horizon tasks, such as repository-level coding, through hundreds of think-act steps, yet the experience each run produces is rarely reused on the next. Prior memory systems concentrate on retrieval, finding the most relevant past trajectory. Retrieval cannot observe the running agent, so it cannot decide whether the agent needs an experience, at which point, or for how long. We introduce REM (Reusable Experience Memory), a framework that manages the memory lifecycle from inside the agent's think-act loop through three explicit decisions. What to store: each completed trajectory is consolidated into a phase-structured document, two orders of magnitude smaller than the trajectory. When to recall: the document is injected at the start of the task; the costlier implementation record is withheld until an in-loop gate detects the agent struggling. What to forget: the record is evicted after a single exposure. On repository-level bug fixing (SWE-ContextBench Lite), REM retrieves the related trajectory more accurately than every state-of-the-art memory system (68.7% vs. 55.6% match@1) and improves, in every replicate, end-task resolution (27.6% vs. 24.9%) at 17% lower cost. Injecting the same experience as a summary or raw trajectory, even when oracle-retrieved, does not. Ablating any of the three decisions reduces resolution. Altogether, these results demonstrate that the bottleneck in experience reuse is not retrieval fidelity but how experience is stored and governed across its lifecycle, opening a control-theoretic perspective on agent memory.

papers.title_en: Muffin - A Shared Memory Buffer for Asynchronous AI Agents
papers.authors: Ping-Lin Kuo, Suman Navaratnarajah, Christian Frey, Gresa Shala, Josif Grabocka
papers.evidence: 基于共享记忆缓冲区、面向异步智能体的智能体间协议
papers.tldr: 多智能体在目标驱动推理中常因交互协调时关键信息交换低效而失败，且同步轮流辩论成本高。MUFFIN采用异步智能体框架：编排器按推理需求路由查询，并将高难度任务委派给多智能体，共享内存缓冲区异步交换中间发现，同时保留各智能体私有推理。实验在20个基准设置中17个取得最佳准确率，较现有多智能体辩论提升19.2个百分点且减少77.4% token，无需共享完整轨迹。该协议以更低成本改善信息协调，为异步AI智能体协作提供了新范式。
papers.abstract_en: The rise of Agentic AI systems has changed the landscape of artificial intelligence by enabling strong reasoning capabilities through specialized multi-agent interaction with structured self-reflection. However, in target-driven reasoning tasks, single- and multi-agent systems are often on par in terms of performance gains. A major challenge is that failures often arise from an ineffective exchange of critical information during inter-agent interaction and coordination. Different from existing multi-agent debate paradigms that rely on synchronous turn-taking and sharing information across different agents, we propose an inter-agent protocol based on shared Memory bUFFer INference - referred to as MUFFIN - in an asynchronous agentic framework. In the first step, an orchestrator routes queries based on their reasoning demands and delegates demanding ones to a multi-agent setting, where a shared memory buffer provides asynchronous exchange of intermediate findings while an agent's private reasoning remains local. Our experiments show that our framework Muffin outperforms established competitors, achieving the best accuracy in 17 out of 20 of our benchmark settings, and provides a better quality-cost trade-off than multi-agent debate: Muffin improves accuracy by 19.2 accuracy points while using 77.4% fewer tokens, without requiring full-trace sharing.

papers.title_en: KVStream: Adaptive Parallel Storage Management for KV Caching in Large-Scale LLM Serving
papers.authors: Avinash Maurya, Jaiaid Mobin, Jie Ye, M. Mustafa Rafique, Franck Cappello, Bogdan Nicolae
papers.evidence: 面向智能体负载的KV缓存前缀检索跨存储层调度
papers.tldr: 长上下文 LLM 服务中 KV 缓存超出 GPU 与主机内存，前缀检索的存储 I/O 成为推理关键路径。KVStream 将前缀检索视为跨存储层的聚合带宽调度，批量读取、延迟写回、各层副本并按空闲自适应认领未读块。接入 LMCache 后，检索达到理论上界的 5% 内，离线吞吐最高提升 1.49 倍，突发请求下平均 TTFT 最多降低 6.1 倍。该工作无需预测或调参即可利用多级存储并行带宽。
papers.abstract_en: Long-context LLM serving for agentic, coding, and document workloads reuses prefixes whose key-value (KV) cache outgrows GPU and host memory, putting storage I/O on the critical path of the inference step for retrieving prefixes. A single node-local NVMe absorbs all retrievals, while the parallel file system or cloud file store that nodes already mount carries almost no inference traffic. We cast prefix retrieval as aggregate-bandwidth scheduling across these tiers and present KVStream, a KV cache engine that batches a step's reads, defers writes behind the forward pass, replicates each chunk on every tier, and lets each tier adaptively claim the next unread chunks once it is free. Our performance model shows this routing attains the aggregate-bandwidth bound without prediction or tuning, whereas any static split misses it by a margin that grows as per-tier bandwidths drift or fluctuate. It also predicts that the time-to-first-token (TTFT) gain grows with load, as faster retrieval drains the queue, and disappears when host memory or arrival order keeps reuse in cache. Plugged into LMCache and evaluated on four models, six datasets, and up to 128 GPUs, KVStream retrieves within 5% of the bound, delivers up to 1.49$\times$ higher offline throughput than LMCache, and lowers mean TTFT by up to 6.1$\times$ under bursty arrivals.
